title: Cybersecurity & AI Security
summary: Where machine learning meets defense, using AI to detect, explain, and get ahead of attacks rather than just react to them.

meta.problem: Traditional signature-based security tooling struggles against novel, fast-evolving attacks, and black-box ML detectors that do catch them are often too opaque to trust or act on.
meta.motivation: Coming from a background in explainable AI for medical diagnosis (see the Biomedical AI chapter below), the same instinct applies here: a detection system a security analyst can't interpret is a system they can't fully rely on.
meta.currentWork: Just beginning: coursework and lab onboarding with CYBER-CARE this term. This page will grow into a real research narrative as the work does.
meta.futureDirections: Explainable ML-based intrusion and anomaly detection; adversarial robustness of security classifiers.

title: Transportation & CAV Security
summary: Securing the connected and automated vehicles, V2X links, and intelligent transportation infrastructure that Houston's roads increasingly run on.

meta.problem: Connected and automated vehicles extend a city's attack surface onto public roads: a compromised V2X message or ITS controller isn't just a data breach, it's a physical safety risk.
meta.motivation: This is the core of what drew me to UH and CYBER-CARE: cybersecurity research with an immediate, physical-world stake, in a city where transportation infrastructure is actively being modernized.
meta.currentWork: Just beginning: reviewing the CAV/V2X security literature and identifying an initial thesis-scale problem within CYBER-CARE's transportation security agenda.
meta.futureDirections: Threat modeling for V2X communication; anomaly detection for connected-vehicle networks; resilience of ITS control systems under attack.

title: Federated Learning & Privacy-Preserving ML
summary: Training useful models across vehicles, sensors, or institutions without ever centralizing the raw data.

meta.problem: Transportation and healthcare data alike are often too sensitive or too distributed to centralize, but centralization is what most ML pipelines assume.
meta.motivation: A natural extension of working with sensitive medical imaging data during my BSc: the privacy constraints there and in connected-vehicle telemetry rhyme more than they differ.
meta.currentWork: Just beginning: surveying federated learning approaches for adversarial robustness and privacy guarantees relevant to CAV and ITS data.
meta.futureDirections: Federated intrusion detection across vehicle fleets; differential privacy guarantees for shared transportation models.

title: Post-Quantum & Quantum Cryptography
summary: Preparing today's cryptographic infrastructure, including the systems that will secure tomorrow's connected vehicles, for a post-quantum world.

meta.problem: Widely deployed public-key cryptography is vulnerable to sufficiently large quantum computers, and long-lived infrastructure (transportation systems included) needs to migrate well before that threat materializes.
meta.motivation: A longer-horizon complement to the applied security work above: the systems being secured today need cryptographic foundations that will still hold in fifteen years.
meta.currentWork: Just beginning: building foundational knowledge in lattice-based and other post-quantum cryptographic schemes.
meta.futureDirections: Post-quantum key exchange for resource-constrained V2X devices; migration strategies for legacy transportation-security infrastructure.

title: Blockchain & Decentralized Security
summary: Decentralized trust models for coordination between vehicles, infrastructure, and institutions that don't share a single trusted authority.

meta.problem: Connected-vehicle and cross-institution data sharing often needs verifiable trust without a single central authority everyone agrees to rely on.
meta.motivation: A natural pairing with the federated-learning thread: decentralized learning and decentralized trust are two sides of the same coordination problem.
meta.currentWork: Just beginning: exploring where blockchain-based trust and integrity guarantees are actually load-bearing versus where they're unnecessary overhead.
meta.futureDirections: Blockchain-backed integrity verification for V2X message logs; decentralized identity for connected-vehicle networks.

title: Cyber-Physical Systems Security
summary: The connective thread across all of the above: wherever software decisions have physical-world consequences.

meta.problem: Cyber-physical systems fail differently than pure software systems: a bad decision doesn't just corrupt data, it can move a vehicle or misdirect infrastructure.
meta.motivation: The umbrella framing for the whole research direction above: every one of these threads is ultimately a cyber-physical systems security problem viewed from a different angle.
meta.currentWork: Just beginning, alongside the threads above, as part of onboarding with CYBER-CARE.
meta.futureDirections: To be defined as the more specific threads above mature.

title: Bachelor's Thesis: Lung Nodule Classification
summary: A transfer-learning ensemble for classifying lung nodules from CT images, with explainable AI layered on top, later extended into a published paper.

meta.problem: Lung nodule classification models are often accurate but opaque, limiting clinical trust in their output.
meta.motivation: An early interest in making AI decisions inspectable rather than just performant, the same instinct now carried into security research.
meta.methods: Transfer learning with an ensemble of pretrained CNN backbones, combined with explainable AI (XAI) techniques to surface which image regions drove each classification.
meta.datasets: LIDC-IDRI (Lung Image Database Consortium and Image Database Resource Initiative) CT dataset.

title: UGC-Funded Project: ASD Detection
summary: Automated Autism Spectrum Disorder detection using a single-stage CNN, funded by the University Grants Commission.

meta.problem: Early ASD screening benefits from fast, accessible automated tools that can flag cases for clinical follow-up.
meta.motivation: Applying computer vision to a diagnostic gap with real clinical relevance in a resource-constrained setting.
meta.methods: YOLOv8-based single-stage CNN for detection, with dataset preprocessing to handle class imbalance.

title: AI Lab Project: Lung Cancer Prediction
summary: A novel ensemble learning model with a high-performance filtering stage, built for lung cancer risk prediction.

meta.problem: Single-model predictors can be brittle across noisy clinical data; ensembling with a strong filtering stage improves robustness.
meta.motivation: Groundwork that fed directly into the bachelor's thesis and eventual LungCT-NET publication.
meta.methods: Ensemble learning combined with a high-performance filter designed to reduce noise before classification.
